anytime_first_td_scorer#u1.description: Rules text for all seven series is silent on whether overtime touchdowns count toward count props (KXNFLTD/ANYTD/2TD) and ordinal props (FIRSTTD/TEAMFIRSTTD/NEXTTD), on credit for laterals/fumble-recovery TDs and on stat-correction timing; only the protected clause mentions overtime (for participation).
anytime_first_td_scorer#u1.what_would_resolve: Obtain full untruncated rules (the sample is cut at 600 characters) or a settled OT game for each series and record the OT and attribution treatment.

anytime_first_td_scorer#u2.description: KXNFLNEXTTD is now known to be the k-th TD of the game (e.g. 4th), but the listing time is not visible; if markets for later ordinals list in-game after earlier TDs, their probability depends on live score, possession and field position, which no pregame input here supplies.
anytime_first_td_scorer#u2.what_would_resolve: Pull open/close timestamps of KXNFLNEXTTD markets by ordinal from Kalshi market history; if listed in-game, define a live game-state input or exclude them from pregame modelling.

anytime_first_td_scorer#u3.description: Pregame coach intent for goal-line packages and opening scripts is unobserved; history gives only realized plays on few drives per season, so first-TD scorer shares have large irreducible error.
anytime_first_td_scorer#u3.what_would_resolve: Own capture of beat-writer reports and practice-observation notes timestamped pregame, evaluated for incremental accuracy over xTD shares.

anytime_first_td_scorer#u4.description: Motivation and rest effects on goal-line roles (clinched teams, tanking, injury-managed vets) have no defined input here, and no data shows how large they are for scorer shares.
anytime_first_td_scorer#u4.what_would_resolve: Define a rest/role-change flag from late-season snap histories and test on weeks 16-18.

anytime_first_td_scorer#u5.description: Participation and personnel data used for goal-line personnel trees (nflverse participation from NGS, roughly 2016-2023, later FTN) gives a short and partly broken history, and a nflverse game-day inactives loader was not confirmed; inactives may need scraping ESPN or Pro-Football-Reference.
anytime_first_td_scorer#u5.what_would_resolve: Verify the current nflverse participation/snap-count/inactives loaders and their seasons; if inactives are absent, test a scrape of the official game-day inactive list and record the coverage window.

anytime_first_td_scorer#u6.description: No model-free first-drive script data exist before 2016 and the TD-allocation of a team's first TD (drive 1-3) rests on few observations per team-season, so the allocation factor of the team-own first-TD contract has large irreducible estimation error.
anytime_first_td_scorer#u6.what_would_resolve: Pool scripted-opener outcomes across coach tenures and measure the shrinkage constant by out-of-sample log-loss on first-TD scorers.

anytime_first_td_scorer#u7.description: KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD text does not say how a team's first touchdown scored by its defence or special teams is handled (whether it settles the 'No <team> Touchdown' strike NO with all named players NO, or an unnamed 'other' strike), which changes the residual mass for offensive players.
anytime_first_td_scorer#u7.what_would_resolve: Find a settled TEAMFIRSTTD market where the team's first TD was a return/defensive score and read its settlement.

combos_and_parlays#u1.description: Rules text now exists for all six series, but none states how a voided/postponed leg, a tied moneyline leg after overtime, a push on an integer line, or a KXNFLCOMBO player who is not 'a participant in both halves' is handled (the PREPACK, PREPACK2ML and PREPACK3ML texts are complete and simply silent; only the KXNFLCOMBO leg list is cut off in the sample).
combos_and_parlays#u1.what_would_resolve: Obtain full untruncated rules for PREPACK, PREPACK2ML/3ML and KXNFLCOMBO, or settled examples with a tied/voided leg or a player exit, and record the treatment per leg type.

combos_and_parlays#u2.description: Historical sportsbook same-game-parlay prices and their implied correlations are proprietary; this limits evaluating whether a correlation model beats the dealer's.
combos_and_parlays#u2.what_would_resolve: Purchase or capture SGP quotes (paid feeds) for a season and compare modelled joint to quoted price.

combos_and_parlays#u3.description: Whether to use a copula, a drive-level game simulator, or a latent-factor model for the joint is undecided; each handles identities and regime dependence differently and no test exists here.
combos_and_parlays#u3.what_would_resolve: Run a held-out comparison of joint log-likelihood on 2022-2025 same-game leg sets (research step, not performed here).

combos_and_parlays#u4.description: Shared weather as a combo dependency is not defined: wind moves total, kicker and passing legs together but the shape and thresholds by leg pair are not specified.
combos_and_parlays#u4.what_would_resolve: Define leg-pair weather elasticities from games with measured wind and test on dome versus outdoor splits.

combos_and_parlays#u5.description: The combo layer needs leg marginals from the sibling archetype models (spread, total, QB yards, TD scorer); those outputs are not yet defined as a common interface, so marginal calibration is an undefined cross-archetype dependency.
combos_and_parlays#u5.what_would_resolve: Define per-leg marginal probability outputs and a shared latent-state sample (margin, total, availability) from the game-level model that sibling archetypes expose.

combos_and_parlays#u6.description: KXNFLNBA needs an NBA championship probability that no NFL input produces; the cross-league leg input is defined only as an import of the NBA catalog model, whose output format, as-of convention and calibration are not yet agreed.
combos_and_parlays#u6.what_would_resolve: Define a shared cross-sport futures output (team, as-of time, P(title)) in the NBA catalog and validate it before pricing the combo.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u1.description: All 34 series now have rules text, but quarter and half total/spread/winner/team-total texts (KXNFL1Q-style and KXNFL1H/1HTOTAL/1HSPREAD/1HTEAMTOTAL/2H/2HTOTAL/2HSPREAD) are silent on postponement, KXNFLPREPACK1HFT does not say whether its full-game leg includes overtime or how a full-game tie settles, and KXNFLNOSCOREQ/HIGHSCOREQ do not state the postponement rule.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u1.what_would_resolve: Obtain full untruncated rules or a settled example (postponed game, tied full game) for these series and record the treatment.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u2.description: Overtime treatment is inconsistent between two 2nd-half winner series: KXNFL2H includes overtime while KXNFL2HWINNER settles on regulation only; whether this is intended or a template difference that could be corrected mid-season is unknown, and pricing the two as the same event would be wrong.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u2.what_would_resolve: Confirm with current listings of both series (rules text at order time) and settled examples from an overtime game.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u3.description: How much per-drive scoring really differs between periods after opponent adjustment is unestablished; small samples may make period-specific rates indistinguishable from game-level rates.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u3.what_would_resolve: Out-of-sample comparison of period-specific vs shrunk game-level rates on 2022-2025 quarter totals (research step, not performed).

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u4.description: Real-time tempo and timeout intentions at half end (coach-level policy for running down the clock versus pushing for a score) are not published; only realized behaviour is visible.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u4.what_would_resolve: Derive coach-level end-of-half policy from clock/timeout/score states and test predictive value.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u5.description: Role-level personnel effects on period scoring are not defined: it is unclear whether a missing RB or TE changes Q1 scripts more than Q4.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u5.what_would_resolve: Define a depth-chart-aware team strength per period and test on games with missing starters.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u6.description: Weather that changes during the game (rain or wind arriving in the second half) affects period-specific kicking share and passing efficiency, but only one game-time observation exists in nflverse and no pregame forecast of the change time is archived, so the period-specific weather increment cannot be fitted.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u6.what_would_resolve: Capture hourly NWS forecasts and observed hourly conditions for stadium locations for at least one season and fit the period-by-weather interaction.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u7.description: The sampled period rules only say 'Only points scored during the 1st Quarter of play count'; attribution of a score completed after the clock expires (untimed down, extra point after the gun) and scoring on a play that starts before the boundary is not stated, so period boundary handling is inferred from official scoring-play periods.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u7.what_would_resolve: Ask the exchange or sample a settled market with a boundary-timed score to confirm that the official scoring-play period governs.

first_half_and_quarter_totals#u8.description: nflverse schedules and pbp expose who received each kickoff but a toss-winner and receive/defer decision field was not confirmed; team deferral habit (the ex ante driver of nfl.opening_possession) may need Pro-Football-Reference game pages or manual capture.
first_half_and_quarter_totals#u8.what_would_resolve: Inspect nflverse column lists for toss fields and test a scrape of the PFR toss line; if neither exists, treat opening possession as a coin flip pregame with a small deferral-habit term.

first_score_team_time_race#u1.description: Rules text now exists for all three series, but KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME's sampled strike shows only the overtime bucket: regulation bucket boundaries, the game-clock convention and the settlement when no TD is scored at all are not stated; KXNFLRACE rungs other than 35 were not sampled.
first_score_team_time_race#u1.what_would_resolve: Pull the full strike list of a live KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME event and KXNFLRACE event from the Kalshi markets endpoint and record bucket edges and rungs.

first_score_team_time_race#u2.description: Scripted openers are not observable before kickoff; only realized early drives are available, and sample sizes per team (about 17 first drives per season) limit precision.
first_score_team_time_race#u2.what_would_resolve: Aggregate multi-season first-15-play scripts and coach continuity; test whether script persistence survives coordinator changes.

first_score_team_time_race#u3.description: Whether a drive-level renewal model or a direct hazard model of scoring by game minute better predicts first-TD timing is unresolved, and dependence between teams' early drives (defence adjusting) is untested.
first_score_team_time_race#u3.what_would_resolve: Out-of-sample comparison of both on bucketed first-TD times (research step, not performed here).

first_score_team_time_race#u4.description: Role-level availability (specific linemen, receivers) effects on opening-drive scoring have no defined input, and QB status alone may be insufficient.
first_score_team_time_race#u4.what_would_resolve: Define a starter-weighted early-drive efficiency and test on lineup-change games.

first_score_team_time_race#u5.description: Rule-regime and officiating effects on early field position and penalty-affected opening drives are not defined into any input beyond kick-return statistics.
first_score_team_time_race#u5.what_would_resolve: Quantify the effect of touchback spot changes and crew penalty rates on first-drive outcomes.

first_score_team_time_race#u6.description: Receive/defer decision and toss winner (the driver of nfl.opening_possession deferral habit) are not confirmed to exist in nflverse schedules or pbp, which expose only who received each kickoff; the stated source cannot be assumed to build the input.
first_score_team_time_race#u6.what_would_resolve: Check nflverse column lists for toss fields and test a PFR scrape; otherwise use realized kickoff receiver and treat toss as a coin flip pregame.

game_events#u1.description: Whether the 2026 regular-season overtime format guarantees both teams a possession is not confirmed by the sampled rules text or by any retrieved source; the tie hazard depends heavily on it. The regulation-OT margin lattice is also not limited to 0, 3 and 6: with both teams possessing, a TD plus extra point or two-point try leaves margins of 1 and 2, which changes P(level | OT).
game_events#u1.what_would_resolve: Retrieve the 2026 NFL rulebook OT section and record the adopted format and effective season.

game_events#u2.description: Rules text now exists for all seven series, but KXNFLGAMETD and KXNFLTEAMTD do not say whether overtime touchdowns count (TOTALTD does), KXNFLTEAMTD does not say whether defensive/return TDs count, and KXNFLDSTTD does not say how fake-punt or fake-FG TDs are classified.
game_events#u2.what_would_resolve: Obtain full untruncated rules or settled overtime examples for GAMETD/TEAMTD and a settled DSTTD market with a trick-play score.

game_events#u3.description: The relative contribution of end-of-regulation management versus pure scoring lattice to regulation ties is unmeasured; if behaviour dominates, game-level models need coach-specific states.
game_events#u3.what_would_resolve: Backtest regulation ties against lattice-only predictions by coach policy tercile.

game_events#u4.description: Safeties are rare (a few percent of games) so team-level rates have extreme sampling error; no public dataset gives pressure and exposure at team-play granularity before 2016 with tracking-quality labels.
game_events#u4.what_would_resolve: Pool league-wide per-play safety probabilities and test whether team factors add skill.

game_events#u5.description: After the reconciliation the TD-count series KXNFLTOTALTD, KXNFLGAMETD and KXNFLTEAMTD and the D/ST TD series belong here (stages g4, g5); families named in the archetype such as period TDs, team/game stat thresholds and both-teams-score still have no live series here and no stage, so no coverage is claimed for them.
game_events#u5.what_would_resolve: If series for period TDs or team/game stat thresholds are listed, add a stage per family (period TD lattice, team-stat count model) reusing the team TD and drive inputs.

game_events#u6.description: Per-play pressure and protection data for the safety hazard (pass-rush win rate against end-zone drop-backs) is not in nflverse pbp, which holds exposure (yardline_100 >= 95) and safety flags only; public availability of pressure charting by play is unconfirmed and charting vendors are paid.
game_events#u6.what_would_resolve: Check NGS/PFF/SIS pressure fields for public exposure and licensing, and test whether exposure plus team sack rate alone predicts safeties out of sample.

game_moneyline_spread#u1.description: KXNFLGAME now has rules text (ties pay $0.50 per team), but the KXNFLSPREAD text does not say whether overtime points count toward the margin or what happens on postponement, and KXNFLWEEKHIGH is TITLE_ONLY so dead-heat splitting and the week definition are unverified. The OT margin lattice is wider than 3, 6 and 0 when both teams possess.
game_moneyline_spread#u1.what_would_resolve: Obtain full untruncated KXNFLSPREAD rules (or a settled OT game) and sample a listed KXNFLWEEKHIGH market.

game_moneyline_spread#u2.description: KXNFLPROBOWL says the NFC/AFC must win the 'Pro Bowl flag football game', but does not say whether points earned in Pro Bowl Games skills events carry into that game's score, and KXNFLPROBOWLWIN has no rules text; the format's history is only a few games, so the roster-strength input is weakly identified.
game_moneyline_spread#u2.what_would_resolve: Read the NFL's Pro Bowl Games scoring rules for the season and a settled KXNFLPROBOWL market; sample KXNFLPROBOWLWIN rules.

game_moneyline_spread#u3.description: The heavy-tail shape for margins above 28 points is estimated from few games (a handful per season); whether it depends on mismatch size or is nearly constant is not resolved.
game_moneyline_spread#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate generalized Pareto parameters on 25 seasons and test for covariate dependence.

game_moneyline_spread#u4.description: Position-level point weights for the lineup-adjusted rating depend on player grades or win-rate metrics (PFF, ESPN), whose public availability and licence terms are not verified.
game_moneyline_spread#u4.what_would_resolve: Confirm access and licence for the player performance indices, or build in-house EPA-on-field versions.

game_moneyline_spread#u5.description: Fitting position-slot weights by ridge on availability indicators needs consistent historical injury-report and inactive vintages; nflverse holds weekly final injury statuses only, so historical weights are fitted on realised availability while pregame use depends on forecast designations, a mismatch of unknown size.
game_moneyline_spread#u5.what_would_resolve: Capture daily injury-report vintages for a season and compare weights from realised availability with weights from Friday designations.

game_total#u1.description: KXNFLBOTH counts overtime points, but the sampled KXNFLTOTAL and TOTALPRECISE texts (a complete primary sentence followed only by the trademark disclaimer) do not state whether overtime points count or a postponement rule; OT inclusion changes about 6-7% of games' totals.
game_total#u1.what_would_resolve: Obtain the full rules text for live KXNFLTOTAL and TOTALPRECISE markets or a settled overtime game's final total settlement.

game_total#u2.description: Pregame weather forecast vintages are not archived publicly, so the forecast-error component of the weather effect cannot be estimated historically without own capture or a paid archive. Until capture exists the dose-response is fitted on observed wind and temperature, so measurement error from forecast uncertainty is not estimable and the pregame_knowable label for the weather response stays partial.
game_total#u2.what_would_resolve: Start capture of forecast vintages for each game at 24h and 3h, or purchase an archive from a weather vendor.

game_total#u3.description: The size and direction of coach tempo and aggression effects on totals are not separated from team efficiency; whether a coach-level tempo variable adds beyond team neutral pace is untested.
game_total#u3.what_would_resolve: Add coach-level tempo and 4th-down aggression to the plays model and compare out-of-sample.

game_total#u4.description: Heavy-tail behaviour near 98.5 points (a record-scale total) is barely estimable from data: by unverified recollection only a very few NFL games (e.g. the 1966 Washington-Giants game and a 2018 Rams-Chiefs game) have exceeded that level, and the count has not been checked against nflverse results; ladder rungs there are dominated by model form.
game_total#u4.what_would_resolve: Count games with total > 98.5 and the upper-tail frequencies directly from nflverse results since 1999 and older records, then treat extreme rungs as probability floors from a conservative tail form.

game_total#u5.description: KXNFLBOTH (each team >=35, OT included) is staged on catalog nfl.paired_score_covariance_own, whose measurement is a binned linear residual correlation of the two scores; dependence in the joint upper tail at N=35 can differ from the body correlation, and no tail-specific estimate is defined yet.
game_total#u5.what_would_resolve: Extend the paired-score input with empirical P(both>=N) versus product of marginals for N in 28-42 by model-total bin (or a survival copula) and test calibration on held-out seasons.

off_field_events#u1.description: Only KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE remains TITLE_ONLY (value definition: total, APY or guarantees, and the horizon unknown); KXNFLHIRECOACH does not say whether 'a coach' means head coach only, and KXNFLPRIMETIME's flex and postponement treatment is truncated in the sample.
off_field_events#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE rules and the full untruncated KXNFLHIRECOACH and KXNFLPRIMETIME texts.

off_field_events#u2.description: A timestamped archive of insider reports linked to official acts does not exist publicly; conversion rates by reporter tier cannot be estimated without paid social-listening data or own capture.
off_field_events#u2.what_would_resolve: Capture reports going forward and backfill with a paid archive; assess conversion rates by reporter.

off_field_events#u3.description: Several events (celebrity signings, ownership stake sales, stadium completion) have no reference class, so base-rate approaches are unreliable and may need judgemental priors.
off_field_events#u3.what_would_resolve: Define per-series reference classes or exclude series with no usable class.

off_field_events#u4.description: Weather delay now has an input, but international venue-retention risk (KXNFLGAMELOCATION: security, stadium readiness, weather) and celebrity-signing events (KXNFLHKANE, KXNFLCOMPETE) still have no physical or behavioural driver input beyond base rates.
off_field_events#u4.what_would_resolve: Define per-series inputs (historical relocation frequency of international games, celebrity tryout-to-signing reference class) or accept base-rate treatment explicitly.

off_field_events#u7.description: A structured transactions wire (signings, trades, cuts, retirements with timestamps) is not confirmed to exist in nflverse, and scraped sources (Pro-Football-Reference, Spotrac/OverTheCap) and social archives carry terms-of-service and coverage risk, so the history behind the event hazard inputs may not be reproducible.
off_field_events#u7.what_would_resolve: Inspect nflverse loaders for a transactions table and test the legal and technical access of PFR, Spotrac and an official league transaction page; record coverage by season.

player_availability#u1.description: Only KXNFLWEEKSTART remains TITLE_ONLY (which positions, chart vs snap); the WEEKCOMPETE text does not say whether a special-teams snap counts, and EVERYWEEKCOMPETE does not say explicitly whether games missed while on a reserve list (IR, suspension) break the streak; KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2 does not say which of its injured-but-listed and inactive-players clauses governs an injured, listed, inactive QB2.
player_availability#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNFLWEEKSTART rules and a settled EVERYWEEKCOMPETE market for a player who spent time on IR; confirm ST snaps with a settled WEEKCOMPETE case.

player_availability#u2.description: Timestamped injury-report vintages (Wednesday, Thursday, Friday) are not preserved in public datasets, which blocks historical calibration of designation to participation at the exact report times.
player_availability#u2.what_would_resolve: Start capturing reports at publication or buy a historical vintage feed, then backfill.

player_availability#u3.description: The incumbent-versus-challenger QB gap is now defined (nfl.qb_challenger_prior), but its calibration for rookies and late-round QBs rests on a draft-slot regression and a few preseason dropbacks; whether draft capital or coach statements dominate the benching hazard is untested.
player_availability#u3.what_would_resolve: Define the gap with a prior built from draft capital and pre-draft grades; test on QB-weeks 2010-2025.

player_availability#u4.description: RETURN and WEEKCOMPETE for a retired, unsigned or long-term injured player depend on retirement, signing and activation decisions; nfl.non_roster_return_status defines the transition model but its comeback base rate rests on a small reference class and no verified source of retirement-intent signals.
player_availability#u4.what_would_resolve: Count comebacks and signings of retired or unsigned veterans from the transactions wire since 2000 to fix the base rate, and validate the insider-interest flag on past cases.

player_availability#u5.description: KXNFLDEBUT is titled 'Player to Make Debut' but its sampled rules use the first-start-as-QB wording; other strikes of the same series (a true first appearance or snap) may exist with a different settlement and are not visible in the single sample.
player_availability#u5.what_would_resolve: Sample several KXNFLDEBUT markets and confirm whether any use a participation definition of debut.

player_availability#u6.description: A nflverse game-day inactives loader and a nflverse transactions table were not confirmed; depth-chart publication timing within the week is not preserved in weekly depth-chart snapshots, and official practice-day injury vintages are unarchived.
player_availability#u6.what_would_resolve: Check nflverse loader lists for inactives and transactions, scrape the official inactive page for a test season, and begin timestamped depth-chart and injury-report capture.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u1.description: KXNFLPASSINT now has rules text, but KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS is TITLE_ONLY (career window, strike and whether postseason TDs count unknown), and no sampled text states whether overtime statistics count for the standard TD/INT props or how stat corrections are handled.
qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS rules and the full untruncated PASSTDS/PASSINT text or a settled overtime game.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u2.description: Turnover-worthy throw rate and pressure-to-throw detail come from PFF or Sports Info Solutions charting and Next Gen Stats; their licences, history length and field definitions are not verified here, and public nflverse lacks them. The nflverse ff_opportunity expected-pass-TD columns used as an alternative source for xPassTD are also not confirmed field by field.
qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u2.what_would_resolve: Confirm the data vendor, licence terms and available fields, or construct in-house proxies.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u3.description: The extent to which the QB's own goal-line rushing displaces passing TDs after controlling for team pass rate is unestablished and may depend on the specific QB and coach.
qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate a QB-level goal-line sneak/run rate model and test marginal effect on passing TDs.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u4.description: Rest or benching incentives for QBs in meaningless late games or development plans for rookies are not captured by any input; the effect on play time in weeks 17-18 is unmeasured.
qb_passing_tds_and_ints#u4.what_would_resolve: Define a clinched-and-resting flag for QBs and test it on weeks 17-18.

qb_passing_yards#u1.description: None of the six rules texts (passing yards, attempts, completions, H2H) say whether overtime statistics count or which statistics provider is the source of truth; the existing draft asserted regulation-and-overtime without text support.
qb_passing_yards#u1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full contract terms for the passing series, or the settlement of a passing market in a game that went to overtime compared with the regulation-only statistic.

qb_passing_yards#u2.description: Coverage shell and per-play pressure for the current season are not in free open data during the season (participation is published after the postseason); in-season pressure must come from QB-level PFR weekly counts or FTN rusher counts, and coverage from paid charting (PFF, SIS), so the pressure and leakage matchup is coarser than the record's design.
qb_passing_yards#u2.what_would_resolve: License one charting vendor (PFF or SIS) or build approximations from sack, hit and scramble flags and test how much signal is lost.

qb_passing_yards#u3.description: How to estimate a quarterback's benching rule is data-thin: only a handful of lopsided games per coach per season exist, and the rule is probably also tied to the quality of the backup and injury rest; the shrinkage constant and window are guesses.
qb_passing_yards#u3.what_would_resolve: Back-test the pull-threshold model on 5 seasons and compare calibration of attempt forecasts for favourites by coach with and without it.

qb_passing_yards#u4.description: Situational and schedule factors (Thursday short weeks, travel across time zones, clinched-seed rest) affect quarterbacks' yardage only weakly in the literature, and the size of the effect on passing yards specifically is not established here.
qb_passing_yards#u4.what_would_resolve: Attach nfl.rest_travel and nfl.divisional_familiarity to this archetype and test whether they add explanatory power to attempts and yards after volume and script are in the model.

qb_passing_yards#u5.description: Every per-game ladder text refunds only a QB who is 'active' but never plays (PRECISE: never takes a snap; PASSYDS/PASSATT/PASSCOMP: never appears in a live play); none says what happens if the named QB is inactive or scratched before kickoff, while the H2H text refunds players who do not enter the game.
qb_passing_yards#u5.what_would_resolve: Pull the full Kalshi rules PDF or an expired market's settlement of a scratched QB to see whether an inactive QB refunds or resolves No.

qb_passing_yards#u6.description: Checked the nflreadr dictionaries: was_pressure and time_to_throw exist only in pbp_participation (2016+; NGS to 2022, FTN from 2023) and that table is released after the postseason, so the current season has no free play-level pressure flag; PFR advanced passing (2018+) gives weekly QB pressure counts and FTN charting (2022+, within 48 hours) gives pass rushers and blitzers. Still unverified: per-season null rates of was_pressure and which PFR pressure fields are week-level.
qb_passing_yards#u6.what_would_resolve: Load pbp_participation and load_pfr_advstats(stat_type='pass', summary_level='week') for 2018-2025 and count non-null pressure fields per season and per week.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u1.description: Overtime handling, the statistics source of truth and the correction policy are not stated in any receiving rules text; 1 of the 12 live series (KXNFLLONGESTREC) is title-only, so its strike construction and settlement are unknown (see u6).
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u1.what_would_resolve: Archive full rules for each series and compare settled values against the game book for overtime games.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u2.description: Route-level participation and shadow-coverage assignments are proprietary (PFF, SIS) or tracking-only (NFL NGS full data); the record does not assume free play-by-play carries routes run (open-data access unverified, see u5), so TPRR for most players may have to be approximated from targets and snaps.
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u2.what_would_resolve: License a charting vendor or approximate routes from pass-play snap participation and test the loss in explanatory power.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u3.description: The final series assignment keeps KXNFLRRYDS (combined rushing plus receiving yards) and KXNFLMOSTRECYDS (game-most receiving yards) in this archetype. Stage s8 now covers them, but the within-game covariance of a back's carries and targets (substitutes in some schemes, complements when he is the lead back in a pass-heavy trailing script) is not estimated.
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate the player-game correlation of rushing and receiving yards for backs by role and script bin on 2016-2025 data and use it in the s8 sum.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u4.description: No schedule or motivation input exists for receivers: late-season starter rest, short-week route participation and trade-deadline role changes are plausible drivers with unmeasured size.
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u4.what_would_resolve: Test adding rest and clinch flags to route-share models using three seasons of data.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u5.description: Checked the nflreadr dictionaries: no free table carries per-player routes run. pbp_participation lists every offensive player on the field per play (pass-play snaps are a route proxy that includes pass blockers) but its route field is only the primary receiver's route, and for 2023+ it is published after the postseason; FTN charting (2022+, in-season) has no route or alignment field. nfl.routes and targets-per-route-run are therefore paid-vendor (PFF, SIS) or a prior-season snap proxy; alignment remains unverified.
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u5.what_would_resolve: License PFF or SIS route data, or measure how much a pass-snap-on-field proxy from prior-season participation loses against vendor routes for TPRR forecasts.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u6.description: KXNFLLONGESTREC has no rules text, so the value a player with a live play and zero receptions takes (0 yards, void or No), the activation rule and the strike construction are unknown; the rules-sampled sibling KXNFLLONGREC has left this archetype.
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u6.what_would_resolve: Capture KXNFLLONGESTREC rules_primary/rules_secondary from a listed market, or the settlement of an expired KXNFLLONGESTREC market for a player who recorded no catch.

receiving_yards_and_receptions#u7.description: The four scalar receiving texts (KXNFLESCALATORREC, KXNFLESCALATORRECYDS, KXNFLLADDERREC, KXNFLLADDERRECYDS) define payouts on official receptions or yards but contain no non-participation, inactive or postponement clause, unlike the binary rungs, so a scratched receiver's scalar position may settle at zero.
receiving_yards_and_receptions#u7.what_would_resolve: Settlement record of an expired receiving escalator or ladder market for a receiver ruled inactive, or Kalshi's full scalar-market terms.

rushing_yards#u1.description: None of the eight rushing rules texts (binary rungs, scalar escalator and ladder, attempts, longest rush, H2H, game-most) address whether overtime rushing yards count or name the statistics source of truth.
rushing_yards#u1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full contract terms for the rushing series, or the settlement of a rushing market in an overtime game compared with the regulation-only statistic.

rushing_yards#u2.description: Run-gap, run-location and defenders in the box are only partially present in free data; yards before contact and blocking scheme labels are paid (PFF, SIS), so the OL and front-match inputs are partly estimated from outcome data.
rushing_yards#u2.what_would_resolve: License a charting source or test an outcome-only proxy for run direction and box count.

rushing_yards#u3.description: The RB committee share model does not separate coach preference from reactivity to performance and fatigue within a game, so within-game share evolution is not well specified.
rushing_yards#u3.what_would_resolve: Fit a within-game carry-allocation model on 5 seasons of data and compare against a static pre-game share.

rushing_yards#u4.description: Workload and rest effects across weeks for runners are not defined here and the literature on consecutive-game workload is mixed.
rushing_yards#u4.what_would_resolve: Add cumulative touches and days-since-last-game features and test on holdout seasons.

rushing_yards#u6.description: The sampled KXNFLRSHYDSPROT text uses overtime only to define 'participates after the first half'; it does not say whether overtime rushing yards count toward the rung, and the text is truncated before the clause for a player with no first-half play. The earlier claim that overtime is included for statistics is unsupported.
rushing_yards#u6.what_would_resolve: Read the full protected-contract text and an expired market that went to overtime to see whether overtime yards counted and how a player with no first-half snap settles.

rushing_yards#u7.description: The weather by run-style interaction asserts that zone/power offences gain and finesse runs lose yield in bad weather, with no evidence from sampled rules or data; the sign of the yield effect is a hypothesis.
rushing_yards#u7.what_would_resolve: Estimate yards per carry by wind and precipitation bin split by scheme labels over several seasons and check that the sign differs by scheme before using the interaction.

rushing_yards#u8.description: Checked the nflreadr dictionaries: defenders_in_box and was_pressure are in pbp_participation (2016+; 2023+ FTN data released after the postseason, so not for the current season), n_defense_box is in FTN charting (2022+, charted within 48 hours) and NGS rushing gives a weekly per-rusher share of 8+ defender boxes. Still unverified: per-season null rates and whether FTN box counts match the participation definition.
rushing_yards#u8.what_would_resolve: Load pbp_participation and ftn_charting for 2022-2025, compare defenders_in_box with n_defense_box on shared plays and count non-null rows per season.

rushing_yards#u9.description: The KXNFLESCALATORRSHYDS and KXNFLLADDERRSHYDS texts define payouts on official rushing yards but contain no non-participation, inactive or postponement clause, unlike the binary rungs; whether a scratched back's scalar position settles at zero yards or is refunded is not stated.
rushing_yards#u9.what_would_resolve: Settlement record of an expired rushing escalator or ladder market for a back ruled inactive, or Kalshi's full scalar-market terms.

season_awards#u1.description: Six series remain title-only (KXNFLOROY, KXNFLDROY, KXNFLOPOY, KXNFLDPOY, KXNFLCOACH, KXNFLHOFINDUCTEES); the 21 rules texts name the awarding body for most awards but none states ballot close dates or how a shared annual award settles a named candidate's market.
season_awards#u1.what_would_resolve: Capture rules text for the six title-only series and compare the NFL-titled award series with their AP-titled twins at settlement.

season_awards#u2.description: The final series assignment moved the Draft and interception-leader series out and kept the Hall of Fame and Top 100 series here. Stage s8 covers them, but the Hall of Fame committee's internal reduction from finalists to the class (the order of cut votes and the 80 percent approval threshold) and the Top 100 voting procedure (how many players vote, ballot form) are recalled, not verified.
season_awards#u2.what_would_resolve: Read the Hall of Fame selection bylaws for the 2027 class and the NFL Top 100 methodology note, and fit finalist-to-inductee rates on 2010-2026 classes.

season_awards#u3.description: The AP panel size, ballot close date relative to the final regular-season week and the tie method are recalled from public descriptions and not verified against current AP documentation.
season_awards#u3.what_would_resolve: Check the AP's published voting rules for the current season and compare with historical vote tables.

season_awards#u4.description: Public straw polls are not stored in structured archives; capturing them requires manual curation or news APIs, and the voter-sentiment signal has a short history.
season_awards#u4.what_would_resolve: Build a weekly capture of public straw polls from three outlets and evaluate their predictive value against final votes over multiple seasons.

season_awards#u5.description: KXNFLROTM text says 'for October of the 2026-27 NFL season' but not whether the window is the calendar month or the league's week-block definition of a monthly award; nfl.award_month_window_games counts 3-5 games from the schedule on an assumed definition, so the primary windowing input is unconfirmed.
season_awards#u5.what_would_resolve: Check the NFL's published Rookie of the Month window definition and the Kalshi full rules; recompute window games from the confirmed definition.

season_awards#u6.description: Straw-poll capture has no cited structured archive (manual), Pro-Football-Reference scraping terms were not checked, and per-voter ballots are mostly not public, so the split-penalty and exposure inputs can only be fit to published vote totals and not to individual ballots.
season_awards#u6.what_would_resolve: Check the PFR terms of use and robots policy, locate any structured straw-poll archive, and confirm which vote breakdowns the AP publishes by voter.

season_awards#u7.description: The AP MVP and other annual award ballot format (single first-place plurality versus ranked-points) was not checked against current AP rules and the sampled Kalshi text names only the winner; this changes how vote splitting and second-place support matter.
season_awards#u7.what_would_resolve: Fetch the current AP award voting rules and an expired MVP market's resolution text to confirm the ballot format and tie rule.

season_awards#u8.description: KXNFLCOTY and KXNFLEXECOTY list 'Tie/Co-Winners' as a separate outcome, but the texts do not say whether a named candidate who shares the award resolves Yes, No or 1/N, so a co-winner scenario cannot be priced for either the candidate or the tie market.
season_awards#u8.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full terms for the award series or the settlement of a past shared AP or PFWA award market.

season_awards#u9.description: KXNFLPROOTY (Protector of the Year) and KXNFLWPMOTY name no awarding body; the Protector award's electorate, eligibility (linemen only or any blocker) and criteria are not known here, so nfl.ol_individual_protection_record is built on an assumed lineman-only, pass-protection definition.
season_awards#u9.what_would_resolve: League or sponsor announcement describing the Protector of the Year voting body, eligibility and criteria, checked against the first winners.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u1.description: Career markets show no expiry date (they may close before a retirement); KXNFLLEADERPINT, KXNFLCAREERRSHTDS and KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS are title-only; no rules text states overtime treatment, the statistics source or stat-correction handling for season totals.
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u1.what_would_resolve: Fetch each series' market close and expiration dates and full rules from the Kalshi API, and compare settled season totals with official league statistics.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u2.description: The within-season persistence of role and the size of regime-change shocks are assumed (ICC of 0.1-0.3 and a 25 percent shift threshold) and not estimated here; they largely determine the width of season-total distributions.
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u2.what_would_resolve: Estimate variance components and shift hazards on 2012-2025 weekly data and compare calibration of threshold probabilities.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u3.description: How the open field of unlisted contenders is treated for position-wide leader markets is undefined: a leader contract resolves over every player, but only a few have market contracts, so the field's residual mass needs a tail model.
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u3.what_would_resolve: Backtest a field model that includes all players with at least 50 percent of the leader's snaps on historical leader outcomes.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u4.description: Transaction and coaching-change timelines are not available as a clean structured free dataset, so the regime-change hazard must be built by manual curation and has limited event counts for rare events like in-season coordinator changes.
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u4.what_would_resolve: Curate a dated event log for 10 seasons from official transaction wires and press releases.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u5.description: Checked nflreadr: load_trades (trades only), load_injuries (weekly report status since 2009) and load_depth_charts (weekly since 2001) exist, but no loader for general transactions (IR moves, signings, releases) or coordinator changes was found among the functions checked, so nfl.role_regime_change_hazard needs manually captured events.
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u5.what_would_resolve: Check the nflverse release list for a transactions or coaching table; if absent, plan manual capture from NFL transactions pages and team press releases and label the data own_capture.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u6.description: Team-level season totals and extremes are now staged (s9), but head-to-head season comparisons between two players (paired covariance of two season totals) are not modelled by this chain, and the ICC 0.1-0.3 and 25 percent shift threshold remain assumptions (u2).
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u6.what_would_resolve: Add a team-level stage or a separate archetype for team season leaders and head-to-head comparisons, and estimate the ICC and shift threshold from 2012-2025 player-weeks.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u7.description: KXNFLSEASONRSHYDS (rules sampled, Saquon Barkley 1500+) and KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS (title-only) share the title 'Rushing Yards'; whether they are one series under two tickers or distinct ladders cannot be told from the sample (carried over from the rushing record).
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u7.what_would_resolve: Fetch both series' markets from Kalshi and compare strikes, players, seasons and expiry.

season_player_stats_and_leaders#u8.description: The KXNFLTSPEC rules text is truncated after defining team passing yards as net of sack yardage, so definitions for other team statistics (rushing yards, touchdowns, sacks) and any tie or postponement rule for team-special markets are not visible.
season_player_stats_and_leaders#u8.what_would_resolve: Full KXNFLTSPEC rules_secondary from a listed market or Kalshi's contract terms page.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u1.description: Tie treatment is now stated only in the per-team WINS-* and EXACTWINS* texts ('Ties do not count as wins'), whose sampled markets refer to the 2025-26 season; the main KXNFLWINS and KXNFLWINS-ANY texts omit any tie or postponement rule, so whether they follow the same convention for 2026-27 is not confirmed.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u1.what_would_resolve: Rules text for a 2026-27 per-team win-total market and for KXNFLWINS/KXNFLWINS-ANY, or settlement of a past market in which the team had a tie.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u2.description: Opponent-adjusted team ratings from vendors (DVOA, PFF) are paid and the free alternatives (EPA from nflverse) are noisier; the preseason prior needs roster-level talent data (contracts, snaps) that is only partially free.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u2.what_would_resolve: License a vendor rating or build an EPA-based rating and compare out-of-sample accuracy.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u3.description: How a new head coach or play-caller changes a team's expected win rate is not quantified; the literature on coaching change effects is inconclusive and the catalog has no input for it.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate a coaching-change effect from 2002-2025 team-season data after controlling for roster change.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u4.description: The league's division and wild-card tiebreak ladders (head-to-head, division record, common games, conference record, strength of victory, strength of schedule) are recalled from public descriptions and not verified against the current rulebook, yet KXNFLDIVISIONORDER and KXNFLWORSTTOFIRST explicitly settle on them.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u4.what_would_resolve: Read the current NFL tie-breaking procedures and verify the simulator against past seasons' published final standings.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u5.description: The archetype mixes win totals, seeds, division and title futures, last-to-win, last-undefeated, streak, wins-by-week and multi-season contracts; all are read from one simulation, and although every series now has rules text, the sequence contracts' bye and same-week conventions have not been implemented or tested in the simulator.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u5.what_would_resolve: Implement the weekly-grid conventions (byes, same-week ties, tie results) and reproduce past last-undefeated and last-to-win outcomes from historical schedules.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u6.description: KXNFLROUNDQUAL ('qualifies for the divisional round') has only a primary rule sentence; it does not say whether the #1 seed, which has a bye and plays no wild-card game, counts as qualified, which shifts the contract probability by roughly the probability of the #1 seed. The natural reading counts the bye team as qualified (it plays in the divisional round); the record prices both readings until the text is confirmed.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u6.what_would_resolve: Read Kalshi's full rule or an expired round-qualifier market where a bye team was involved to see how a bye team settled.

season_win_totals_and_futures#u7.description: Several rules texts are a single sentence (KXNFLAFCCHAMP, KXNFLPLAYOFF, KXNFLSEED, KXNFLAFCEAST) with no postponement, cancelled-game or forfeit clause; a season with an uncompleted game (as in 2022) would leave standings, seeds and division winners undefined under the contract text.
season_win_totals_and_futures#u7.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full terms for season futures, or the settlement treatment applied to markets affected by the 2022 cancelled Buffalo-Cincinnati game.

team_total#u1.description: The KXNFLTEAMTOTAL rules text does not say whether overtime points count, gives no postponement/cancellation rule and names no source of truth; the regulation-only versus full-game pmf choice therefore cannot be fixed from the contract.
team_total#u1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi's full contract terms or rulebook entry for KXNFLTEAMTOTAL, or a settled overtime game's market result compared with the regulation and final scores.

team_total#u2.description: The correlation between a team's points and its opponent's points (through pace, script and shared weather) feeds the team-total pmf through script; its size by game-total regime has not been estimated at the level of a bivariate score distribution.
team_total#u2.what_would_resolve: Fit a bivariate score model on 2009-2025 games and compare this team's upper-tail rung frequencies under independent versus correlated score-pair draws.

team_total#u3.description: Intraday quarterback and line status relative to kickoff and in-game exits cannot be reconstructed from free weekly data; the quote-time availability vintage must be captured prospectively.
team_total#u3.what_would_resolve: Start a timestamped capture of official reports and inactives and measure late-news frequency.

team_total#u4.description: Schedule and motivation effects on a single team's scoring (short week, clinched-seed rest) have no attached input, and their size relative to opponent and pace effects has not been measured.
team_total#u4.what_would_resolve: Add rest and clinch indicators to the drive lattice and test the incremental fit.

team_total#u5.description: Checked the nflreadr pbp dictionary: td_team, safety, fourth_down_converted, two_point_attempt, two_point_conv_result, field_goal_result and kick_distance exist in nflfastR play-by-play (there is no fg_distance field; kick_distance is the field-goal distance). Still unverified: how soon after each game the current-season file is refreshed (the quote-time vintage, u3); the backup-quarterback point loss of 4-7 is also an unsourced estimate.
team_total#u5.what_would_resolve: Record the nflverse pbp release timestamps against game end times for several weeks, and estimate the backup-versus-starter points gap from 2015-2025 games.

team_total#u6.description: The merged catalog definitions of nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean (measurement: 'KXNFLBOTH counts overtime') and nfl.paired_score_covariance_own (mechanism, rationale and output: the both-teams-35 joint tail) still describe KXNFLBOTH, which was re-filed to game_total; the review cannot change merged definitions, so the stale text is disclosed in each input's why.
team_total#u6.what_would_resolve: A catalog-side edit (integrate pass) that rewrites both definitions for the single-team KXNFLTEAMTOTAL use, or a game_total review that takes ownership of the joint-tail definition.

unreg:combine_testing_results#u1.description: The fastest-40 rules sample has no tie clause and neither sample names a source of truth or says whether unofficial broadcast times or later official times settle.
unreg:combine_testing_results#u1.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi contract terms or a settled tied/revised market showing which time and payout were used.

unreg:combine_testing_results#u2.description: Pre-draft speed-camp training effects between the college season and the Combine are unmeasured, so the pre-Combine prior may be biased for prospects from specialised facilities.
unreg:combine_testing_results#u2.what_would_resolve: Training facility per prospect linked to the gap between college track marks and Combine 40.

unreg:combine_testing_results#u3.description: Collegiate GPS top-speed data are not public and attempt-level Combine results are inconsistently published, limiting both the prior and the attempt-noise estimate.
unreg:combine_testing_results#u3.what_would_resolve: A licensed tracking feed or consistent attempt-level archives from the league.

unreg:combine_testing_results#u4.description: It is unverified whether the NFL.com tracker exposes the unofficial-versus-official flag and timestamps needed to estimate revision size historically.
unreg:combine_testing_results#u4.what_would_resolve: Inspect the tracker during the next Combine and archive snapshots.

unreg:combine_testing_results#u5.description: The start year of comparable electronic 40-yard timing (the record text says about 2006; Combine times are commonly described as electronically timed from about 1999) and any later timing-system or start-trigger changes are not verified from a source.
unreg:combine_testing_results#u5.what_would_resolve: League or tracker documentation of timing systems by year, or a break test on yearly best 40 times across candidate years.

unreg:combine_testing_results#u6.description: Series KXNFLCOMBINE is titled only 'NFL Combine' and only the broad-jump 148-inch market was sampled; sibling markets on other drills (vertical, bench press, 3-cone, shuttle) may exist and would need different pools (linemen for bench) and priors that this record does not cover.
unreg:combine_testing_results#u6.what_would_resolve: List all markets in KXNFLCOMBINE and sample their rules text; add archetype coverage for any drill other than broad jump and 40.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u1.description: KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD now have rules text (single game, inclusive buckets, zero TD = NO), but whether return TDs use return yards from the catch spot, how a 0-yard recovery TD is recorded, and whether regular-season listings share the Super Bowl wording are not visible.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample a regular-season listing of each series and compare settled buckets with official play-by-play for games containing return TDs.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u2.description: The kick-distance convention for KXNFLLONGESTFG (spot of kick, line of scrimmage plus end-zone depth and holder setback) is not stated; official distance may differ by a yard or two from a constructed measure. Whether a fair-catch free kick, scored as a field goal, counts as a made field goal for KXNFLLONGESTFG is also not stated.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u2.what_would_resolve: Compare official gamebook field-goal distances with computed values on a sample of 60+ yard kicks.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u3.description: Kicker ball speed, hang time and pregame practice distances that would identify who can reach 70 are not public; the ceiling tail leans on kickoff proxies and career max makes.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u3.what_would_resolve: Capture pregame warm-up distances from beat reports or obtain tracking-vendor ball-speed data.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u4.description: Own-1 snap counts and Hail Mary versus kick policy change with rule shifts (kickoff regime, punting strategy), so the historical exposure rate may not carry over; the 99-yard sample is only a handful of events.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u4.what_would_resolve: Recompute exposure after each rule change and pool by era; use a prior on the tail with a stated posterior uncertainty.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u5.description: KXNFLLONGESTPLAY says 'a play from scrimmage of at least 99 yards'. Interception, fumble and missed or blocked FG returns occur on scrimmage downs and can run 99-109 yards; whether they count is not stated, and the two readings need different exposure inputs.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u5.what_would_resolve: A Kalshi rules clarification or a past settlement involving a 99+ yard return; until then price both readings.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u6.description: KXNFLLONGREC describes active-no-play (fair price) and played cases, but not a player ruled inactive or a game postponed; it is also unclear whether a reception nullified by penalty is excluded from 'longest reception recorded'.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u6.what_would_resolve: Sample more KXNFLLONGREC listings and check settled outcomes for inactive players and nullified catches.

unreg:extreme_play_length#u7.description: The post-2025 kicking-ball preparation era and touchback-to-35 kickoff rules have one to two seasons of data, so the era shift in 60+ yard attempt and make rates is estimated from a small sample and may keep moving.
unreg:extreme_play_length#u7.what_would_resolve: Re-estimate the era effect after each season with a hierarchical prior and report the posterior interval on P(70+).

unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u1.description: The sampled rules text is truncated before the full scoring table (kicker and bonus rules), and Sleeper's API fields for kicker and defence scoring, historical corrections and group membership are not verified here.
unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u1.what_would_resolve: Capture the full rules text and test the Sleeper endpoints for stat fields and a week of known scores.

unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u2.description: Kicker and defence fantasy scores (a kicker's over 9.2 market is in this series) follow field-goal and extra-point opportunity and drive stalls, a different process from skill-position scoring that this chain only touches in one stage.
unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u2.what_would_resolve: Author a separate kicker chain with drive and distance inputs and verify kicker scoring weights.

unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u3.description: Opponent and matchup inputs (def_epa, dvp, coverage, run defence) are now attached to the yield stage, but how much of a player's fantasy variance they explain beyond role and script has not been measured.
unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u3.what_would_resolve: Add defence-versus-position and coverage inputs and test incremental explanatory power by position.

unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u4.description: Historical vintages of Sleeper's published values (final, corrected) and Sleeper's group membership by date are not publicly archived, so settlement-error rates cannot be estimated from history.
unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u4.what_would_resolve: Begin a weekly capture of Sleeper points and group membership and use it to quantify correction frequency.

unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u5.description: The KXNFLFFPTS rules text is truncated before the kicker, defence and bonus scoring table, the ladder says 'standard Points Per Reception' while other series say full-PPR, and overtime and correction sentences appear only in some series' text, so one scoring rule cannot be asserted for all twelve series; KXNFLFANTASYMOST uses ESPN PPR scoring instead of Sleeper.
unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u5.what_would_resolve: Fetch the full rules text for each series (scoring table and wording) and compare Sleeper's published kicker and defence scoring.

unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u6.description: KXNFLFANTASYMOST names ESPN's FFL PPR scoring but not which ESPN settings (default league settings change over time), whether 'full game' includes overtime points, what happens to an inactive named player, when ESPN's value is read or whether later stat corrections apply; the sample is for a past (Feb 2026) game.
unreg:fantasy_points_markets#u6.what_would_resolve: Rules text of a current KXNFLFANTASYMOST market plus ESPN's published default PPR scoring settings for the season, checked against a settled market.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u1.description: KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK have no listing and no rules; by title they duplicate KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS and KXNFLDRAFT1, but tie, round and trade handling cannot be confirmed for them.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample rules text if these tickers list; until then treat them as unverified aliases.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u10.description: Public consensus boards thin out beyond about 150-300 prospects, so late-round slot, school-count and last-pick-position probabilities rest on position base rates rather than prospect-level rankings.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u10.what_would_resolve: Capture deep boards (300+) from several outlets and measure late-round rank-to-pick dispersion on past drafts.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u2.description: The league position label at selection settles Nth-at-position and last-pick series; Edge versus DT versus LB and safety/corner swaps diverge from college and board labels, and the label source at the time of selection is not archived.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u2.what_would_resolve: Collect rules text and compare league labels to board labels on historical hybrid players.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u3.description: Team-private draft boards, medical grades and trade negotiations are not public, so decision-maker intent can only be inferred from reports and history.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u3.what_would_resolve: No public resolution; quantify insider-report accuracy by outlet and carry the residual as uncertainty.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u4.description: Point-in-time vintages of consensus boards are not archived publicly in the form needed (timestamped by date); coverage of NFL Mock Draft Database history is unverified.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u4.what_would_resolve: Verify the vendor archives or start own capture of public boards for several drafts.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u5.description: The trade-up frequency for picks 1-5 rests on a small number of drafts with heavy dependence on the individual quarterback class, so the trade hazard is imprecise; the Supplemental Draft has too few events for a stable model.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u5.what_would_resolve: Pool more drafts with era effects and report posterior intervals; treat Supplemental Draft as a base-rate model only.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u6.description: Consensus boards and mock drafts increasingly anchor on sportsbook draft odds close to the draft, so a market-derived signal can enter through nfl.draft_board and the slot dispersion model; no public archive tags which boards are odds-informed.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u6.what_would_resolve: Own-capture boards with methodology notes and test board-versus-odds correlation by days to draft; use pre-odds vintages.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u7.description: Only KXNFLDRAFTTEAM states that an undrafted player resolves NO; for exact-slot, top-5, over/under, Nth-at-position and matchup series (including neither matchup player drafted) the non-declare or undrafted case is not written.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u7.what_would_resolve: Check settled outcomes of past markets on undrafted or returning players, or obtain a rules clarification.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u8.description: No sampled text addresses draft postponement or cancellation, or a Supplemental Draft that is not held (KXNFLSDRAFTTOP rules_secondary is empty).
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u8.what_would_resolve: Obtain the Kalshi rulebook clause for postponed or cancelled events and a Supplemental Draft listing with full rules.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u9.description: Trade-hazard levels for top slots and the Supplemental Draft tiered lottery details are stated from general knowledge without a cited source; earlier drafts cited a 30 percent top-10 trade rate and a weighted order that are not verified.
unreg:nfl_draft_selection#u9.what_would_resolve: Compute top-10 trade rates from a trade log of the last 15 drafts and cite the league's Supplemental Draft procedures document.

unreg:slate_extremes#u1.description: No sampled rule names the stat source agency; for the weekly game market the game is tied to its originally scheduled date, but how a postponed or rescheduled game is assigned to a week is not stated.
unreg:slate_extremes#u1.what_would_resolve: Full contract terms or a settled market involving a postponed game.

unreg:slate_extremes#u2.description: Only the 225+ rushing-yard variant of KXNFLGAMESPECIALS was sampled. The rules text refers to quarter-specific markets that exclude overtime, and the series may carry passing, receiving or touchdown rungs; this record has inputs only for rushing, so passing volume, QB efficiency, target share and quarter-window distributions are NOT covered for those variants.
unreg:slate_extremes#u2.what_would_resolve: List every KXNFLGAMESPECIALS market with rules text; if non-rushing or quarter-window variants exist, author a separate player-single-game-stat specials archetype.

unreg:slate_extremes#u3.description: The 109.5 total rung lies beyond all post-merger observations and the 51.5 margin rung has been exceeded only about five times in 50 seasons, so the tail shape for margin and total maxima, and its shift under the current kickoff and scoring regime, is weakly identified; the 225-yard rushing rung is recurring and better identified.
unreg:slate_extremes#u3.what_would_resolve: Bootstrap tail-shape intervals and out-of-sample checks across eras; sensitivity of P(YES) to the shape.

unreg:slate_extremes#u4.description: The coach-level continuation policy after large leads is estimated from few qualifying drives per coach and may be confounded with backup-quarterback quality.
unreg:slate_extremes#u4.what_would_resolve: Hierarchical model separating coach and backup-QB effects, validated on held-out seasons.

unreg:slate_extremes#u5.description: The sampled text does not say how cancelled or no-contest games (for example BUF-CIN in 2022), or postponed games moved across weeks, count toward season thresholds and the weekly argmax markets, nor whether a never-completed game can be the 'highest scoring game'.
unreg:slate_extremes#u5.what_would_resolve: Full Kalshi contract terms or a settled market involving a cancelled or suspended game.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u1.description: KXNFLSBMVPDEF and KXNFLSBMVPQB have no listing or rules; for all four series co-MVP handling, a losing-team winner, returner or kicker classification and the resolution source are not stated in any sampled text.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample rules for the DEF and QB variants once listed and obtain a clarification on co-winner and losing-team cases.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u2.description: Panel ballots, individual votes and exact voting timing (before or after the final whistle) are not public, so the vote model rests on winners only, with about 60 observations.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u2.what_would_resolve: No public resolution; use winner data with shrinkage priors and treat voter timing as a stated assumption.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u3.description: The quarterback premium has changed across eras and with the passing-heavy league; the sample is too small to separate the premium from the skill and script effects, which makes the position priors uncertain.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u3.what_would_resolve: Fit era effects with hierarchical shrinkage and add playoff games of winners as extra training data.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u4.description: Whether the fan-vote weight and panel size documented in public sources match current practice is not verified, and the source for the MVP position label is not stated.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u4.what_would_resolve: Verify with the league's current award announcement and archived articles from recent finals.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u5.description: KXNFLSBMVPQB is titled 'Non QB Championship MVP' but its ticker suffix suggests a QB-YES contract; with no listing, whether YES means a non-QB or a QB winner is unknown.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u5.what_would_resolve: Obtain the listing's yes_sub_title and rules text when the series lists.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u6.description: Neither sampled text gives the close time; if markets trade during the game until the announcement, the live ballot-state input and a live feed are required and pre-game inputs become priors only.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u6.what_would_resolve: Record open/close timestamps of the next Super Bowl MVP listings relative to kickoff and the announcement.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u7.description: Pro-Football-Reference coverage of sacks before 1982 (unofficial) and of tackles (unofficial throughout) in Super Bowl box scores is unverified, so the credit model drops those covariates for early games.
unreg:super_bowl_mvp#u7.what_would_resolve: Check PFR Super Bowl box scores for 1967-1981 sack fields and document which covariates are official per era.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.description: This unregistered archetype still groups several mechanism families (per-team counts, both-team counts, score-path functionals, rare play calls, league tie and long-kick counts); the season extremes, streaks, primetime and team-points series have left it, but the remaining grouping should still be split into per-family archetypes.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.what_would_resolve: Split into per-family archetypes and author chains for the player-count, voting and playoff-path markets, reusing the rushing and bracket chains.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.description: The both-team game texts (KXNFLGAMESACK, KXNFL2PTCONV, KXNFL4DCONV, KXNFLNONQBPASS, KXNFLLARGELEAD, KXNFLLEADCHANGE, KXNFLCOMEBACK) have no overtime, postponement or source clause, KXNFLLARGELEAD's band ('between 7 to 10') does not state inclusivity, and KXNFLGAMESACK does not repeat the 2-point-try sack exclusion.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.what_would_resolve: Full rules for current listings of each both-team series, or settlements of past markets in overtime games and with a largest lead exactly on a band edge.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.description: Pressure and quarterback sack-avoidance data come from paid vendors, and the flex scheduling rules and network designations are not available as a clean structured free dataset; quarterback and injury status are attached from the catalog but their intraday vintage is not archived.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.what_would_resolve: License pressure data or test a sack-plus-hit proxy; capture flex announcements over a season.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.description: The non-QB pass and pass-from-the-1 inputs rest on tiny team samples and on roster position labels (a backup quarterback listed at another position, a punter's fake-punt pass), so the event definition in play-by-play may not match Kalshi's 'non-QB' wording and the shrinkage constants are guesses.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.what_would_resolve: Compare play-by-play non-QB pass flags with settled KXNFLNONQBPASS markets and fit shrinkage on 2015-2025 team-games by cross-validation.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.description: KXNFLFG, KXNFLTEAMSACK and KXNFLTEAMYDS say the count is recorded 'during the' named game with a 48-hour postponement rule but no overtime sentence, so whether overtime field goals, sacks and yards count is unestablished.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.what_would_resolve: Fetch full rules or an expired overtime game's settlement for each series to see whether overtime events counted; compare with the team-total record's treatment of the same silence.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.description: Playoff and must-win stakes plausibly raise fourth-down, two-point and trick-play rates (several sampled markets are for a championship game), but no input measures a stakes effect and its size relative to coach tendency and score state is unknown.
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials#u.what_would_resolve: Compare 4th-down, 2-point and non-QB pass rates in playoff versus regular-season games for the same coaches, controlling for score state, over 2012-2025.
